title: Thai Iced Tea with Condensed Milk and Star Anise
summary: Assam tea steeps with cinnamon, star anise and turmeric, is sweetened and chilled, then poured over ice and topped with condensed milk, half-and-half and vanilla.
equipment: fine sieve lined with a paper coffee filter

ingredients.item: strong loose black tea, such as Assam
half-and-half (or 60 ml whole milk mixed with 60 ml single cream)

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Put the tea, cinnamon, star anise and turmeric in the heatproof jug, pour over the boiling water and steep for 15 minutes. A long steep makes the tea strong enough to stand up to the milk.

steps.title: Strain and chill
steps.text: Strain through the lined sieve, stir in the sugar until dissolved and let it cool, then chill for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Mix the topping
steps.text: Whisk the condensed milk, half-and-half and vanilla together in the small jug.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Fill the glasses with ice and pour in the tea to about 3 cm from the top. Slowly pour a quarter of the creamy topping over each, so it swirls down through the tea.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with a straw and stir before drinking.

tips: Line the sieve with a coffee filter to catch the fine turmeric.
Chill the tea fully before pouring over ice, or it melts and dilutes too fast.
Pour the topping over the back of a spoon for neater layers.
Reduce the condensed milk to 70 g for a less sweet drink.
storage: The plain tea keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; add the topping just before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
